The repository uses two well-known agent-instruction filenames simultaneously. `AGENTS.md` is declared the "canonical repository guidance" and contains the full contract (architecture layout, scoring rules, ZFC boundary, verification commands, and behavioral constraints). `CLAUDE.md` is explicitly reduced to a redirect stub that says "Read and follow [AGENTS.md]" and "Do not duplicate those instructions here." This pattern — where `CLAUDE.md` defers to `AGENTS.md` — indicates the project is designed to be driven by multiple coding agents (at minimum OpenAI Codex agents and Anthropic Claude Code) and the dual-filename approach is intentional rather than accidental.

**Hard constraints declared in `AGENTS.md`:**
- `## Hands-off boundaries` enumerates explicit prohibitions: no push/tag/merge/release without authorization; no discard or rewrite of unrelated working-tree changes; no editing of managed marker blocks (`<!-- tom-swe:begin -->` / `<!-- tom-swe:end -->`); keep application behavior unchanged in documentation-only work ([AGENTS.md L138-146](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/sjarmak-codeprobe@6052fec96850a06b18527a9bb8e41243bc1cbdb1/-/blob/AGENTS.md?L138-146)).
- A "Beads" task-management system (`bd prime`, `bd show`, `bd update`) is mandated as the "durable work state" system for agents. Evidence includes a required evidence block before closing any bead (`evidence.artifact_path`, `evidence.reviewer_verdict`, `evidence.reviewer_agent`).
